_about: What's on along the route: sky events, holidays, markets, festivals and seasonal nature. Shown in Loop's 'What's on' card when the date and place match where we'll be. near = [lat, lng] (+ km radius, default 70); no near = anywhere. weekly = days of the week (0 Sun … 6 Sat). minLat = only when we're north of this latitude.

items.title: Southern Taurids peak
items.note: Slow, bright fireballs rather than many meteors. The moon is a thin crescent, so the sky is dark. Look north-east.

items.title: Guy Fawkes night
items.note: Not a public holiday, but towns and backyards let off fireworks.

items.title: Extravaganza Fair · Wānaka
items.note: Travelling fair of vintage, crafts, art and food stalls.

items.title: Remarkables Market
items.note: Local food, crafts, coffee and live music by the lake.

items.title: Northern Taurids peak
items.note: Another fireball shower, just after new moon, so the nights are properly dark.

items.title: Queenstown Marathon
items.note: Thousands of runners between Arrowtown, Lake Hayes and Queenstown. Expect road closures and busy roads that morning.

items.title: Leonids peak
items.note: Fast meteors, but the radiant only rises late from NZ, so expect a handful an hour before dawn. The moon sets around midnight.

items.title: Supermoon
items.note: Full moon at its closest. It looks biggest as it rises over the horizon. A bright moon also washes out faint stars and aurora.

items.title: Lupins in bloom
items.note: Purple, pink and blue lupins along the lakes and the road to Aoraki. Best early morning or evening light.

items.title: Hector's dolphins at Porpoise Bay
items.note: The world's smallest dolphins spend summer in the bay. Watch from the beach or swim, without approaching them.

items.title: Otago Farmers Market
items.note: Up to 65 stalls, rain or shine. Good coffee and breakfast, cash is easiest.

items.title: Geminids peak · best shower of the year
items.note: Moonless skies and you're in the Aoraki Mackenzie Dark Sky Reserve. The radiant sits low in the north from NZ, so expect around 20–40 an hour after midnight. Find a dark spot and lie back facing north.

items.title: School summer holidays
items.note: Kiwi families are on the road until early February. Popular DOC and holiday-park sites fill up, so arrive early or book ahead.

items.title: Lyttelton Farmers Market
items.note: Small harbour-town market with good food stalls.

items.title: Longest day
items.note: Summer solstice. In the South Island the sun sets around 9.40 pm and it stays light until about 10.30 pm.

items.title: Southern rātā in flower
items.note: The bush lights up red on the hillsides, especially around the Otira Gorge and the West Coast side of the passes.

items.title: Christmas Eve supermoon
items.note: The year's closest full moon rises on Christmas Eve.

items.title: Christmas Day
items.note: Public holiday. Supermarkets and most shops are closed, so stock up and fill the tank on the 24th.

items.title: Boxing Day
items.note: Public holiday on Saturday 26, also observed on Monday 28 Dec. Shops reopen (Boxing Day sales); some places keep holiday hours.

items.title: New Year's Eve
items.note: Fireworks at midnight in the bigger towns. Campsites are at their busiest.

items.title: New Year holidays
items.note: Public holidays on 1 Jan and 2 Jan; because the 2nd is a Saturday, Monday 4 Jan is a holiday too. Expect holiday hours.

items.title: Pōhutukawa in bloom
items.note: NZ's Christmas tree flowers red along the North Island coast, often still going in early January.

items.title: La Cigale French Market
items.note: Crêpes, pastries, cheese and coffee. Check the times before you go.
